design_rationale: The study is a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial where subjects were allocated to treatment using a centrally provided computer-generated randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated via a central computer list ensuring adequate sequence generation and allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Recruited subjects were randomized to receive a transdermal patch delivering micro-dose E2 (0.014 mg/day) or placebo for 12 weeks (one patch/week). Randomization was by a centrally provided computer-generated list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind design with matching transdermal patches prevented participants and carers from knowing intervention assignments, and deviations were minimal with an appropriate modified intention-to-treat (full analysis set) analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study was conducted in symptomatic postmenopausal Asian women...

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 160 of 165 randomized participants (97%) with low overall dropout, and missing data imputation using LOCF is unlikely to have substantially biased results given high completion rates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 165 subjects randomized, 81 to micro-dose E2 0.014 mg/day and 84 to placebo; 80 subjects in each group were included in the FAS (Figure 1)... Overall, 14 subjects did not complete the study, four in the E2 group and 10 in the placebo group... To analyze the frequency of hot flushes, the FAS with the last observation carried forward (FAS (LOCF)) was also used.

domain_judgments.rationale: Hot flushes were recorded via standard patient daily diaries, and successful double-blinding ensured that participant self-reporting was not biased by knowledge of treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the screening phase after Visit 1, subjects recorded the daily number and severity of hot flushes on a diary card.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper reports prespecified primary and secondary efficacy and safety variables analyzed according to a defined statistical analysis plan without indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy variable was the relative change in the frequency of all hot flushes from baseline to week 12. Secondary efficacy variables included relative changes in frequency of all hot flushes from baseline to weeks 4 and 8 and frequency of moderate to severe hot flushes from baseline to weeks 4, 8, and 12...

overall_summary: The trial was a well-conducted, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study with central allocation, high retention, and standardized outcome assessments resulting in low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a double-blind randomized controlled clinical trial in which 90 participants were randomly allocated to three intervention groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The method of random sequence generation is not clearly detailed, although allocation concealment using identical tubes labelled A, B, and C is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Random allocation sequence was allowed to randomly enter menopause women. To conceal allocation, all the tubes were prepared the same and were named A, B, C. Those who entered the study randomly received the creams.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blind with identical packaging/tubes, and there is no evidence of deviations from intended interventions or failure of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To conceal allocation, all the tubes were prepared the same and were named A, B, C. Those who entered the study randomly received the creams. Physicians, pathologists, and patients were all unaware of prescribed medications for patients (the study was doubleblind).

domain_judgments.rationale: Around 19% of participants (17/90) were lost to follow-up with differential dropout across groups (3 in lubricant, 8 in Premarin, 6 in royal jelly), and complete case analysis was performed without evidence that missingness was unrelated to the true outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this study, 90 postmenopausal women were divided into three groups consisting of 30 individuals; finally, we had 27 individuals in the lubricant group, 22 in Premarin, and 24 in the royal jelly group (Figure 1). The reason for losing some individuals was not to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated outcome measures (MENQOL and cytology) were used, and both participants and pathologists assessing the cytology were blinded to intervention allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Physicians, pathologists, and patients were all unaware of prescribed medications for patients (the study was doubleblind)... The questionnaire was completed by women residents before and at the end of the intervention period for each of the subjects by individual interviews. Cytological examination of the cervix and vagina was carried out before and after the study and patients’ Pap smear samples were taken at the end of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Registration occurred retrospectively in late 2014 after the study had already concluded (conducted January 2013 to January 2014), and there is insufficient detail to rule out selective reporting of outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered at the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (http://www.irct.ir) with the IRCT code: 2014112220043n1.

overall_summary: The trial has some concerns overall due to inadequate description of the sequence generation method, differential loss to follow-up without intention-to-treat analysis, and retrospective trial registration.

design_rationale: The study is described as a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial where participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using permuted blocks generated via a secure web-based database.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was random, concealed via a secure web-based database and computerized dispensing system, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization by permuted blocks of 9 and stratified by site was conducted in a secure Web based database, and implemented via a computerized inventory system for dispensing identical-appearing tablets in bottles and gel in tubes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and study personnel were appropriately blinded using matching placebos, and analysis was conducted following intention-to-treat principles regardless of adherence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants, study personnel, and clinical providers were blinded to treatment assignments. ... A modified intent-to-treat analysis included all randomized participants who provided follow-up QOL, depressive symptoms, or anxiety symptoms data at week 4, week 12, or both, regardless of treatment adherence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up data were available for 97-99% of randomized participants across outcome measures, representing very minimal missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data on one or more domains of the MENQOL were available on 301 women (>99%) at baseline and 298 (99%) at 4 and/or 12 weeks of follow-up. Similarly for the PHQ-8 and GAD-7, data were available on 301 (>99%) women at baseline and 297 (97%) at follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated self-report outcome measures were used and participants remained blinded to their intervention assignments throughout the trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants, study personnel, and clinical providers were blinded to treatment assignments. ... Menopause QOL was specified a priori as a secondary outcome, measured as change from baseline to 12 weeks in the total Menopause-Specific Qualify of Life (MENQOL) questionnaire.

domain_judgments.rationale: Analyses were conducted according to a pre-specified protocol and statistical analysis plan, reporting all planned secondary outcomes and domains without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Menopause QOL was specified a priori as a secondary outcome, measured as change from baseline to 12 weeks in the total Menopause-Specific Qualify of Life (MENQOL) questionnaire. ... Additional prespecified secondary outcomes included sexual functioning assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and the Female Sexual Distress Scale-Revised.

overall_summary: All five RoB 2 domains were judged to have a low risk of bias due to robust randomization, successful double-blinding with matching placebos, negligible missing data, and pre-specified outcome reporting.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly state that participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to the study group (group A) or control group (group B).

domain_judgments.rationale: The study reports 1:1 randomization but does not provide details on sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After the baseline evaluation (T0), the sample was 1:1 randomly divided into two groups: the study group (group A) and the control group (group B).

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was unblinded/open-label with no placebo control, and analysis was conducted only on complete cases (36/48 in group A and 44/48 in group B) rather than by intention-to-treat, with substantial post-randomization dropouts related to intervention assignment and side effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among the limitations of our study, apart from those mentioned above, was the lack of a placebo group. ... However, after the baseline evaluation and randomization, six (12.7%) women from group A withdrew from the study refusing estriol ovule treatment, and six (12.7%) women reported adverse events consisting of vaginal burning occurring during the first week of the vaginal estriol administration. Therefore they also dropped out of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was differential attrition (25% dropout in the estriol group vs 8.3% in the control group) largely due to treatment refusal or adverse effects, and no imputation or sensitivity analysis was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Consequently, 36 and 44 women from group A and group B, respectively, completed the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Key patient-reported outcomes (SF-36 and FSFI) were assessed in an open-label trial without a placebo control, making self-reports susceptible to participants' knowledge of their assigned intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The women had to place a mark on a 0 to 100 scale for each item that best corresponded to their feelings... The women were instructed to answer both questionnaires by the same clinician (S.C.).

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to rule out selective reporting across multiple timepoints and questionnaire subdomains.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The VMI, SF-36, and FSFI total scores obtained at T0 were compared with T1 and T2 scores through paired Student’s t test.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial, unbalanced post-randomization dropouts analyzed only via complete cases (per-protocol approach), coupled with unblinded patient-reported outcome assessments (quality of life and sexual function) in the absence of a placebo group.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial where participants were assigned 1:1:1 to treatment groups using permuted blocks stratified by site via a secure web-based database.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated randomly and concealed using a secure web-based database and computerized dispensing system, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization by permuted blocks of 9 and stratified by site was conducted via secure web-based database, and implemented by a computerized inventory system for dispensing identical-appearing tablets in bottles and gel in tubes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding with identical-appearing placebos was maintained for participants, personnel, and trialists, and an appropriate intention-to-treat analysis approach was implemented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants, study personnel, and clinicians were blinded to treatment assignments. ... The modified intent-to-treat analysis included all randomized participants who provided a baseline MBS score and corresponding vulvovaginal symptom severity at week 4 or 12, regardless of adherence to treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 97% of randomized participants with very low and balanced attrition across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study retention was high: 294 of 302 (97%) women provided primary analysis data (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment was self-reported using standardized scales, and effective blinding of participants prevented bias in reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was severity of the most bothersome symptom (MBS) defined by the participant at trial enrollment as vulvovaginal itching, pain, dryness, irritation, or pain with penetration. Severity was rated 0 to 3, signifying none, mild, moderate, or severe.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov and followed a prespecified protocol and statistical analysis plan with primary and secondary outcomes reported as planned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study protocol (Supplement 1) provides additional details of study procedures. ... clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT02516202

overall_summary: The trial has a low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains due to robust sequence generation and allocation concealment, successful double-blinding, minimal loss to follow-up, and analysis according to a prespecified protocol and analysis plan.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to one of four treatment groups using a computerized random number generator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computerized random number generator was used, no information is provided regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After giving informed consent and being screened for eligibility criteria, subjects were randomized, double-blind, into four treatment groups—DHEA 50 mg daily, conjugated equine estrogen (CEE) 0.625 mg daily (ET), DHEA 50 mg - CEE 0.625 mg daily (DHEA-ET), or placebo—using a computerized program generating random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and placebo-controlled with no reported deviations from the intended protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: subjects were randomized, double-blind, into four treatment groups—DHEA 50 mg daily, conjugated equine estrogen (CEE) 0.625 mg daily (ET), DHEA 50 mg - CEE 0.625 mg daily (DHEA-ET), or placebo

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were reported for all 32 randomized participants (with only minor missing responses on certain questionnaire items), indicating nearly complete follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 32 women randomized, 12 were randomized to DHEA alone, 5 to ET, 9 to DHEA-ET, and 6 to placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed using objective laboratory, MRI, and dynamometry methods, as well as validated instruments, in a double-blind design.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Muscle mass was determined by MRI... Ankle plantar flexor strength and endurance were tested using a Biodex isokinetic dynamometer... Serum was separated from blood at the time of collection by centrifugation and frozen at -70°C

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered protocol or analysis plan was referenced, and multiple outcome measures and analyses were conducted in this pilot study.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Main outcome measures of lower extremity muscle (calf) mass, functional muscle parameters, serum hormone and lipid levels, and quality of life (QOL) were obtained at baseline and after treatment. Statistical analysis compared percent change from baseline values and treatment differences among outcomes.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to a lack of detailed reporting on allocation concealment and the absence of a prospective trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis plan.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where participants were randomly allocated to receive either transdermal estradiol or placebo patches.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial states participants were blindly and randomly allocated, no specific details on the sequence generation or allocation concealment methods are provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The women were blindly and randomly allocated to either transdermal estradiol therapy, 50 \mu g/24 hours, or placebo given as patches twice a week.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blind and placebo-controlled, meaning participants and carers were unaware of the assigned intervention, and there is no evidence of deviations from the intended protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The women were blindly and randomly allocated to either transdermal estradiol therapy, 50 \mu g/24 hours, or placebo given as patches twice a week.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data were minimal (around 8% overall, with 223 of 242 completing the study and analyzed) with reasons documented and balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 242 women were randomized. Three of these were excluded from the analysis as protocol violators... Five women on a regimen of estrogen therapy were withdrawn... Ten of the patients withdrew while receiving placebo... so in the end 223 women completed the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were patient-reported questionnaires collected while participants and personnel were blinded via a placebo control.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The quality-of-life evaluation was performed with self-administered questionnaires, filled in at the clinic, and mailed to an independent nurse for quality control.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospectively registered trial protocol or pre-specified analysis plan is cited, raising some concerns regarding potential selective reporting among the multiple instruments and subscales administered.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The first analysis was based on the overall or total scores. In cases of statistically significant differences p < 0.01 a second analysis was performed in a similar fashion with the subscales or dimensions of the questionnaires.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of detailed information regarding the allocation sequence generation and concealment methods, as well as the absence of a pre-registered trial analysis protocol for multiple quality-of-life instruments.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using a computer-generated schedule in blocks of six to one of three treatment arms.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was generated using appropriate software in blocks of six, and baseline characteristics across groups were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomization schedule was generated with the SAS Proc Plan (SAS Institute, Cary, NC). Women who met the inclusion and exclusion criteria were randomized in blocks of six to 13 weeks of treatment with a vaginal ring delivering the equivalent of 50 μg per day or 100 μg per day E2 or a placebo vaginal ring.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blinded with an identical placebo ring, and analysis followed a modified intention-to-treat approach with no substantial protocol deviations that would compromise intended assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial was conducted at 35 sites in the United States. Healthy postmenopausal women were treated for 13 weeks with a vaginal ring delivering the equivalent of either 50 μg per day E2 or 100 μg per day E2, or a placebo vaginal ring.

domain_judgments.rationale: Differential discontinuation occurred across arms (26.9% placebo vs ~10-12% active), and missing outcomes were handled using last observation carried forward (LOCF), which can bias treatment effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 279 participants (84%) completed the study. Fourteen women in the E2 vaginal ring 50-μg group (12.4%), 11 in the E2 vaginal ring 100-μg group (9.8%), and 29 in the placebo vaginal ring group (26.9%) discontinued treatment. Discontinuation rates were significantly lower in the E2 vaginal ring 50-μg and E2 vaginal ring 100-μg groups than in the placebo vaginal ring group (P = .007 and P = .001, respectively).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were recorded using standard patient diaries and validated scales in a double-blind trial where both participants and outcome assessors were blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Severity of vasomotor symptoms was assessed by a daily diary card and the Greene Climacteric Scale. Urogenital signs and symptoms were evaluated via patient and physician assessment and vaginal cytology.

domain_judgments.rationale: Prespecified primary and secondary outcomes and multiple endpoints are fully reported in accordance with standard regulatory analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was the mean change in the number of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms from baseline to weeks 4, 8, and 12, with last observation carried forward. (Although the study was designed as a 13-week trial, the moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms analysis was done at week 12 to accommodate a request from the US Food and Drug Administration.)

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged to be of some concerns primarily due to differential attrition between the placebo (26.9%) and active groups (9.8-12.4%) combined with the use of last-observation-carried-forward imputation. All other domains were assessed as low risk.

design_rationale: The study was explicitly described as a double-blind randomized controlled trial using computer-generated block randomization to assign participants into two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was randomly generated using computer-generated block randomization and concealed using identical opaque envelopes handled by an independent nurse, with balanced baseline characteristics between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computer generated block of four randomizations was used to randomize participants into two groups in a 1:1 ratio. The allocation and concealment of placebo and the drugs into identical opaque envelopes were done by a nurse who was not involved in contacting with patients or analyzing any data, thus blinding investigators, assessors, cytologist, microbiologist and all participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and personnel were blinded with visually identical placebos, no deviations from the protocol were apparent, and an intention-to-treat analysis with multiple imputation was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The placebo was made by the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Science, Chulalongkorn University and was visually identical to the conjugated estrogens tablet... blinding investigators, assessors, cytologist, microbiologist and all participants... The treatment effect was evaluated with intention-to-treat analysis, with missing data assumed by multiple imputation method.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing data was relatively low (13.4% overall, balanced across arms: 5/34 vs. 4/33) with documented reasons, and intention-to-treat analysis using multiple imputation was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Fifty-eight participants completed the study, all with compliance of > 90% based on pills count on follow up visit... Nine participants, 5 in the estrogens arm and 4 in the placebo arm, discontinued from the study during the 12-week protocol... The treatment effect was evaluated with intention-to-treat analysis, with missing data assumed by multiple imputation method.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was measured using a validated questionnaire (FSFI), objective laboratory and cytological outcomes were assessed by blinded evaluators, and participants were successfully blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The Thai version of the Female Sexual Function Index questionnaire was validated in previous study among Thai postmenopausal women... thus blinding investigators, assessors, cytologist, microbiologist and all participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered in a clinical trial registry before patient enrollment commenced, and reported outcomes align with the pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: Thai Clinical Trial Registry identification number TCTR20180219001, prospectively registered since 2018-02-1911:33:21

overall_summary: The trial was well-conducted with low risk of bias across all five domains, featuring computer-generated randomization, allocation concealment, double-blinding with identical placebos, low attrition handled via intention-to-treat analysis with multiple imputation, and prospective registration.
